subtopics.title: What a Circuit Actually Moves — Charge, Energy and Resistance

questions.question: Current is defined as:
options: The energy carried by a charge
The rate of flow of charge — I equals Q over delta t
The opposition to charge flow
The number of electrons in a wire

questions.question: A potential difference of 18 volts across a resistor means:
options: Eighteen coulombs pass every second
The resistor holds eighteen ohms
Every coulomb passing through hands over eighteen joules
Eighteen electrons are used up per second

questions.question: A battery goes flat because:
options: Its charge is used up by the resistors
The electrons leak out of the wires
The current escapes at the junctions
Its store of chemical energy is spent — the charge itself circulates forever

questions.question: The instrument rules are:
options: Ammeter in series with low resistance; voltmeter in parallel with high resistance
Ammeter in parallel with high resistance; voltmeter in series with low resistance
Both instruments in series
Both instruments in parallel

subtopics.title: Ohm's Law and the Series Circuit — One Path, Shared Current

questions.question: Ohm's law states:
options: V equals I over R
R equals V times I
V equals I times R — potential difference equals current times resistance
I equals V times R

questions.question: In a series circuit the current is the same everywhere because:
options: The battery pushes equally in both directions
There is one path only — charge cannot pile up or leak away
The resistors share it equally
Electrons move faster through bigger resistors

questions.question: For the 18-volt battery with 3 ohms and 6 ohms in series, the total resistance and current are:
options: 2 ohms and 9 amperes
18 ohms and 1 ampere
3 ohms and 6 amperes
9 ohms and 2 amperes

questions.question: The series potential differences split as 6 volts and 12 volts because:
options: A series circuit divides volts in proportion to resistance — twice the ohms, twice the volts
The battery splits its emf equally
The bigger resistor always takes exactly 12 volts
Volts are the same across every series resistor

subtopics.title: The Parallel Circuit — Shared Potential Difference, Divided Current

questions.question: In parallel, the potential difference across each branch is:
options: Divided in proportion to resistance
The full 18 volts on every branch — both branches span the same pair of junctions
Nine volts each
Larger across the larger resistor

questions.question: The reciprocal sum one over 3 plus one over 6 gives one half. The parallel resistance is:
options: One half of an ohm
Three ohms
Two ohms — the reciprocal must be inverted
Nine ohms

questions.question: The parallel total of 2 ohms is smaller than either resistor because:
options: The formula always halves the smallest resistor
Parallel resistors heat up less
The battery works harder in parallel
A second path gives charge somewhere else to go — the combination opposes flow less than either branch alone

questions.question: The branch currents are 6 amperes and 3 amperes, confirming that a parallel circuit:
options: Divides current inversely with resistance — the smaller resistance takes the larger current, and the branches sum to 9 amperes
Sends equal current down every branch
Sends more current through the larger resistance
Uses up current at the junctions

subtopics.title: Series Against Parallel — the Rules, the Traps and the Wiring in Your Walls

questions.question: Same battery, same resistors, yet parallel carries four and a half times the series current because:
options: Parallel batteries are stronger
The connection pattern sets the total resistance — 2 ohms against 9 ohms
Parallel wires are shorter
Series circuits leak charge

questions.question: The memory fix for the swapped-rule trap is:
options: Volts are always the same everywhere
Current is always divided everywhere
Same PATH means same CURRENT; same PAIR OF JUNCTIONS means same VOLTS
The bigger resistor always wins

questions.question: Household appliances are wired in parallel so that:
options: The wiring uses less copper
The total resistance stays high
The breaker never trips
Each receives the full 230 volts and switching one off leaves the others running

questions.question: An overloaded multiplug becomes dangerous because each added appliance:
options: Opens another parallel branch — total resistance falls and total current climbs
Raises the total resistance
Lowers the supply voltage
Reverses the current direction

questions.question: In the taxi picture, volts measure:
options: How many taxis leave the rank per minute
The energy loaded into every taxi — eighteen joules per coulomb
The number of rough patches
The speed limit on the route

questions.question: On the single road, counting taxis at the start, middle and end gives:
options: Fewer taxis after each rough patch
More taxis near the rank
The same number per minute everywhere — taxis are not fuel
No taxis beyond the first patch

questions.question: The rougher 6-ohm patch takes 12 of the 18 volts because:
options: The energy split follows the roughness — double the ohms, double the slice
The first patch always takes less
Volts divide equally on one road
The battery favours the far patch

questions.question: With two roads between the same corners, each route drops:
options: Nine volts each — the eighteen shared
The full eighteen volts — every taxi leaves full and arrives empty
Volts in proportion to its roughness
Nothing until the roads rejoin

questions.question: The traffic splits as 6 amps and 3 amps because:
options: The battery sends taxis alternately
Both roads carry equal traffic
The easy road is the busy one — current divides inversely with roughness
The rougher road attracts more taxis

questions.question: A third plus a sixth gives a half. The whole system's roughness is:
options: Half an ohm
Four and a half ohms
Nine ohms
Two ohms — the upside-down answer flipped back the right way up

questions.question: If your final parallel resistance comes out bigger than the smallest road:
options: You forgot to flip the fraction back
The circuit must be broken
The battery is too strong
That is normal for parallel

subtopics.title: Why Your House Is Wired the Clever Way

questions.question: A house wired in series would mean:
options: Every appliance gets the full voltage
Shared-out voltage, nothing at full strength, and one blown globe darkening the whole house
Lower electricity bills
No need for a distribution board

questions.question: The price of parallel wiring is that every appliance switched on:
options: Dims all the others
Raises the total resistance
Opens another branch — total resistance falls and the total current climbs toward the trip switch's limit
Steals voltage from the lights

questions.question: The wall switch sits in series with its light because:
options: There you want one break to stop everything
Series wiring is cheaper everywhere
Switches cannot be wired in parallel
The light needs less voltage than the plugs
